candidates.claim: refundOrder sorts the amounts as text, so 1000 comes before 250 and the smallest refund is not applied first.
prorate divides by periodDays, so a period of zero days returns Infinity or NaN.
parseDayOfMonth calls parseInt without a radix, so "08" and "09" are read as octal and rejected.
daysBetween gives March 30 days, not 31, because the period bounds are local midnights and the clocks go forward during March.
totalCredit calls reduce without an initial value, so an empty list of credit lines throws a TypeError.
capped compares amount and cap as text, so an amount of "900" with a cap of "1000" contributes 1000.
